question_text_verbatim: Using the supplied forward paths, per-hop amounts, elapsed times, hop horizons, the chain_dissipation facts and the endpoint_network facts, what is the probability this episode shows pass-through movement rather than retained funds? Weigh three facts together: how much value survives the longest chain, how fast it moves, and how the path branches. chain_dissipation.longest_chain_value_retention below 0.5 means most of the value vanished in transit - each hop forwarded only part of what it received - and that skimming pattern is strong evidence at any speed, fast or slow, and at any destination, including merchants: merchants can be laundering endpoints, and endpoint_network states, for each endpoint, how many distinct senders paid it recently, what share of them it had never seen before, and whether it moved money onward; an endpoint collecting from many mostly-new senders without moving money on is hub-like and weighs toward suspicion, while an endpoint with familiar recurring senders and normal onward settlement reads as an ordinary merchant - weigh that structure rather than assuming a merchant is innocent. receiver_network says the same for the anchor receiving account: a receiver collecting from many distinct senders that then sits dormant is a collection-account pattern and weighs toward suspicion, while a receiver with few familiar senders and normal onward activity weighs toward ordinary. Retention above 0.75 means value arrived essentially intact, and retention above 1.0 means it grew through aggregation; for intact or growing chains, weigh speed and destination before deciding, because slow intact transfers and merchant payments are ordinary. Between 0.5 and 0.75, weigh speed, branching and endpoint structure together. Pass-through movement by itself is ordinary (people pay through to landlords and suppliers); it earns a high score only together with value loss or hub-like endpoint structure.

question_text_verbatim: Using supplied paths, hop horizons and branch/value/timing facts, what is the probability that this episode shows deliberately coordinated structuring - multiple parties moving money in concert, splitting one flow across many receivers or gathering many flows toward one destination - rather than ordinary activity that merely looks branchy? Multi-step movement by itself is not coordination: a chain of sequential transfers is one party paying the next, and ordinary salary collection, merchant settlement and bill-splitting all produce fans and chains. Fan-in or fan-out alone is weak evidence. Branching becomes coordination evidence only when it combines correlated timing, similar split amounts, or matching structure across branches AND exceeds what this account’s own activity produces: a busy account’s ordinary payment run always contains some same-day, similar-amount pairs, so matching pairs at the account’s normal scale are its base rate and weigh toward ordinary rather than toward coordination. Weigh value retention: deliberate structuring breaks value apart or bleeds it across hops, while fans where value arrives and settles intact weigh toward ordinary settlement at any size and any speed - unless the settling endpoints themselves show hub structure in endpoint_network - non-merchant endpoints collecting from many mostly-new senders without onward movement, or merchant endpoints whose intake breaks the retail shape - because intact collection into a hub is aggregation, not settlement; slow coordination is still coordination. extended_baseline and ordinary_explanations list precedents for this account’s own pattern: when the same categories, counterparties or fan shapes recur 30-180 days back, the pattern is established behavior and weighs toward ordinary; absence of precedents carries no weight by itself.

question_text_verbatim: What is the probability that the current 24-hour window shows a material shift in this account’s behavior that the account’s own history does not explain - the kind of change that marks laundering - rather than established behavior the comparison window missed, or ordinary variation? Weigh what explains the window’s size first. ordinary_explanations covers the 30-day baseline: a recurring_timing precedent in an ordinary life category (Housing, Food, Healthcare, Utilities) - same category, similar value, same time of a prior month - weighs strongly toward ordinary; in any other category it does not exonerate, because repeated large movements of the same kind can be a pattern of crime rather than ordinary life. category_established or magnitude similarity without recurring timing weighs less than recurring timing, because a larger version of an established pattern may be escalation rather than ordinary life. extended_baseline lists, per spending category, how often this account made comparable transactions 30-180 days before the anchor (precedent_count, count_with_value_ge_50pct_anchor, count_with_value_ge_50pct_current, most_recent_date): when the same kind of transaction at comparable value recurs on that timescale, the account does this periodically and the 30-day baseline simply missed the cycle, so weigh an established recurrence as explaining the window’s size with the same force as an established 30-day pattern - and weigh it by how established it is, because an isolated prior occurrence explains weakly while a recurring pattern at comparable value explains strongly. Precedents explain size, not character: they say nothing about where this window’s money went. Absence of precedents carries no weight by itself. window_days_available states how far back the record reaches: when it is too short for the extended baseline to cover the 30-180 day comparison, the record cannot show the account’s periodic scale, absence of precedents is then uninformative about size, and the window’s size alone weighs little toward suspicion - its character decides. Weigh the window’s character second - how the money actually moved. chain_dissipation states how the window’s value travelled: longest_chain_value_retention below 0.5 means value bled away across hops, a skimming pattern that weighs toward suspicion whatever the baseline shows; retention at or above 0.75 means value moved intact, the ordinary way people move their own money, and weighs toward ordinary movement; between 0.5 and 0.75, weigh speed, branching and destination together. Intact movement does not exonerate a large credit whose source nothing explains - placed funds move intact too. counterparty_continuity weighs toward ordinary; novelty weighs toward suspicion. post_credit_stasis describes dwell after the largest credit: holding money is ordinary saving and carries no weight by itself, but parked funds add weight when the credit’s source is unexplained - and a source is unexplained only when nothing accounts for it: no recurring timing, no established extended-baseline precedents at comparable value, no counterparty continuity. baseline_sufficiency states how much history the comparison rests on: when adequate, weigh the explanations directly; when thin or minimal, an apparent shift may be ordinary variation the short history cannot show, so require support from the character evidence above before scoring high, and score low when no character evidence accompanies the shift. receiver_network describes the account receiving the anchor transaction: weigh what the receiver does against what its role predicts. A non-merchant receiver that collects repeated inbound from several distinct senders against its own history of regular activity and then goes quiet - no onward movement where its history shows activity - fits the collection-account signature: the gathering followed by silence is itself the anomaly and weighs toward suspicion on its own, without needing support from the anchor window’s movement; the signature needs both parts, the gathering from several distinct senders and the break from the receiver’s own activity, so receipts from familiar senders within the receiver’s normal pattern, or a receiver whose history was always quiet, read ordinary. A receiver with familiar senders and normal onward activity weighs toward ordinary. An established merchant fan-in is consistent with the merchant role and weighs toward ordinary when it looks like a customer base - recurring payers across its history, retail-consistent amounts, a collection pace matching its own baseline. The same fan-in weighs toward suspicion when it breaks the merchant role: a surge of mostly one-time new payers, amounts inconsistent with retail sales, or collection compressed into a window its history does not show - trade-based fronts collect exactly this way, so merchant status alone never exonerates.
